source.title: Data Pruning via Moving-one-Sample-out
source.authors: Hao-Ru Tan; Si-Tong Wu; Fei Du; Yu-Kang Chen; Zhi-Bin Wang; Fan Wang; Xiao-Juan Qi

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including references.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates data pruning and reports held-out accuracy after pruning, including robustness tests with synthetic label noise. These results extend the claim to pruning conditions rather than directly testing the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper measures the accuracy impact of selecting and removing training examples, but it does not test memorization of random labels, width scaling, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, optimizer comparisons, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Figure-only comparisons in Figures 1 and 3 are not extracted as numeric rows; textual descriptions of those results are included where they bear on the claim.
record.test_reason: No listed version is tested. MoSo removes examples with low gradient-alignment scores and evaluates pruning performance; it does not remove the most memorized examples as V8 requires. Feldman and Zhang's memorization measure is discussed in related work but is not an experimental baseline. Synthetic label noise does not test V1's paired random-label fitting and generalization claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors propose an empirical-risk-based sample-importance score and an efficient gradient-based estimator that incorporates training dynamics, and report effective classification-data pruning and transfer across architectures. They also state that usefulness is not guaranteed when noise dominates and that evaluation is limited to classification.
record.recipe_differences: This study removes selected training examples to evaluate data-pruning performance. It does not use the interventions or measures in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported pruning performance changes with dataset partition count, surrogate training epochs, and time-step sampling rate; MoSo also outperforms its final-epoch-only variant across pruning ratios.

fits_no_version.finding: MoSo-selected coresets transfer from ResNet-50 scoring to SENet and EfficientNet-B0, matching or outperforming selected pruning baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MoSo coreset selection can transfer across the tested convolutional architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: With 20% synthetic label replacement, MoSo outperforms several difficulty-based pruning baselines but trails Herding by less than one accuracy percentage point.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MoSo retains competitive pruning performance under moderate synthetic label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Training-stage gradient information improves pruning performance over the final-epoch-only variant; lower time-step sampling rates reduce mean performance and increase variance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MoSo selection quality depends on the training-stage information used to estimate its scores.

fits_no_version.finding: Accuracy increases from 74.35 to 75.81 across one to ten scoring partitions. Extending surrogate training from 50 to 200 epochs increases accuracy from 75.76 to 76.58, with a decrease between 100 and 150 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MoSo pruning performance depends on scoring partitions and does not improve monotonically with surrogate training duration.

record.problems: The paper's central comparisons in Figures 1, 3, and 5 are presented as plots without exact values in the text. The pruning experiments report downstream Top-1 accuracy rather than training-versus-test error or the specific outcomes in the listed claim versions. Some experiments compare against baselines, but exact numerical values and uncertainty are generally not provided in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No required version-specific results were available to extract. Figure 1 pruning-ratio comparisons and Figure 4 computational-cost comparisons are outside the listed versions; Figure 1's broad baseline comparisons are described in the text, while exact plotted values are not recoverable. Figure 4 concerns computation time rather than a claim-version result.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fixed random-label fitting and natural-versus-random-label held-out performance under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and remedies for large-batch penalties.
Effects of dropout, training-set size, augmentation, and removing dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor of generalization gaps relative to other measures.
Removing the most memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples, followed by retraining and test-accuracy evaluation.

record.verdict_notes: Held-out accuracy after pruning alone does not test V8: the selection criterion and direction of removal differ. No version-specific verdicts or missing version-specific results are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Network width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measured properties as predictors of generalization gap.
Removing examples specifically identified as memorized and measuring the resulting test accuracy change.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Pruned 80% of CIFAR-100 training data using MoSo-selected samples.
rows.measure: Class-wise accuracy before versus after pruning; Spearman correlation between the two
rows.note: This compares class-wise accuracies, not overall training and test error or a measure named in the claim versions.
rows.check: Class-wise accuracy correlation does not measure any version. The baseline is the full training set, shown as Fullset in Figure 2. This is a diagnostic of the proposed pruning method, not a claim-result row.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Pruned training data using MoSo-selected samples and trained an unseen SENet architecture on the selected data.
rows.note: The text says MoSo consistently outperforms or matches some state-of-the-art methods, but does not give values or a baseline for this specific condition.
rows.check: The evaluated subject is SENet; ResNet-50 supplies selection scores. This compares pruning methods on an unseen convolutional architecture, not convolutional versus fully connected networks. Exclude as a claim-result row.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Pruned training data using MoSo-selected samples and trained an unseen EfficientNet-B0 architecture on the selected data.
rows.note: The text says MoSo consistently outperforms or matches some state-of-the-art methods, but does not give values or a baseline for this specific condition.
rows.check: The evaluated subject is EfficientNet-B0; ResNet-50 supplies selection scores. This compares pruning methods on an unseen convolutional architecture, not convolutional versus fully connected networks. Exclude as a claim-result row.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Pruned training data using MoSo-selected samples on CIFAR-100 with synthetic label noise.
rows.note: The text reports that MoSo performs comparably to Herding and lags by less than 1% Top-1 accuracy, but exact values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: Accuracy after method-selected pruning with 20% label replacement does not establish random-label fitting or removal of memorized examples. This is a pruning-method comparison, not a claim-result row.

rows.note: The text reports that MoSo performs comparably to Herding and lags by less than 1% Top-1 accuracy, but exact values are shown only in the figure.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Compared MoSo pruning with a variant using only the final-epoch gradient.
rows.baseline: MoSo without TDA (using only the final-epoch gradient)
rows.note: The text explicitly states that MoSo outperforms the variant across different pruning rates; this is a data-pruning result, not a test of a listed claim version.
rows.check: The reported advantage concerns MoSo versus its final-epoch-only ablation. Observed is not a valid state for any listed version here; exclude this method-performance comparison as a claim-result row.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Selected a coreset using different MoSo time-step sampling rates.
rows.note: The text says mean performance decreases and variance increases as sampling rate decreases; sampling-rate values are plotted.
rows.check: Sampling rate concerns epochs used to estimate selection scores, not training batch size or another listed intervention. Partial incorrectly treats an estimator tradeoff as a claim effect. Exclude as a claim-result row.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Selected a coreset using MoSo scores computed within partitioned subsets.
rows.note: Table reports the MoSo results for each partition count; the text states partitioning into more subsets can improve performance.
rows.check: The table values are correctly transcribed but compare dataset partitions used for MoSo scoring. They do not measure any version; exclude this method ablation as a claim-result row.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Selected a coreset using MoSo scores after different surrogate-network training durations.
rows.note: The paper says increasing training duration does not uniformly improve performance and that 50 to 200 epochs yields only a 0.82 Top-1 accuracy gain while quadrupling time.
rows.check: The table values are correctly transcribed but vary surrogate training duration for selection scoring. They do not test longer training as a remedy for large batches. Exclude this method ablation as a claim-result row.
